selection_rule_audit.selection_deviation_explanation: Under a strict single-metric argmax on CV Macro-F1 alone, Exp_02 (Word-Only, C=0.15) was the top performer (0.6166). However, the candidate frozen for primary test-set comparison was Exp_06 (Combined, C=0.05, 0.6157) because the experimenter applied composite criteria: Exp_06 achieved the highest held-out validation ROC-AUC (0.6685 vs 0.6571), the lowest Brier calibration loss (0.2322 vs 0.2347), and maintained character n-gram features for sub-word stylometry. This selection rule was composite rather than a strict single-metric argmax.
selection_rule_audit.test_set_isolation: The final test set was strictly locked and was NOT used to select, tune, or adjust any candidate model.

production_decision: The existing production model (62.55% test accuracy, 0.6626 ROC-AUC) is retained without replacement. The candidate models differ by only -6 and +3 correct classifications respectively across 1,370 test samples, exhibiting identical ~0.66 ROC-AUC discrimination. Replacing the production model is not empirically justified.
scientific_limitations_and_disclaimer: Empirical observation: Linear SVM models with n-gram TF-IDF features achieve ~62% to 63% test accuracy on this personal-statement corpus under contributor-grouped evaluation. This represents the empirical behavior of linear n-gram models on this specific corpus and must NOT be interpreted as a universal, theoretical, or definitive ceiling across all possible NLP architectures or datasets. Furthermore, predictions reflect statistical resemblance to benchmark training data and do not establish whether an individual human is lying.
